reflections.summary: Lost despite the turn-1 Gholdengo KO because Whimsicott repeatedly established Tailwind and later Encored Mega Charizard Y into Protect, leaving Tauros free to control the endgame with Rock Slide. The Charizard/Raichu lead was productive, but bringing Kingambit into a Tauros Close Combat position and allowing the Whimsicott-Tauros endgame was unfavorable.
reflections.adjustment: For game 2, reconsider Kingambit as a bring: use Venusaur alongside Charizard/Raichu to pressure Tauros and Milotic more directly, and prioritize removing or denying Whimsicott before using Protect with Charizard. If Charizard is exposed to Encore, attack or switch rather than give Whimsicott a Protect lock.
reflections.notebook: Opponent led Whimsicott + Gholdengo; Whimsicott is a central speed-control and disruption piece, using Prankster Tailwind, Encore, and Taunt. Tauros is the primary Mega Charizard Y answer with Expert Belt Rock Slide and can also delete Kingambit with Close Combat. Opponent used Milotic with Rain Dance, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Protect, Leftovers, and Competitive; it can contest sun and punish stat drops. Against this team, preserve pressure on Whimsicott and avoid leaving Charizard’s last move as Protect when Encore is available. Reassess bringing Kingambit when Tauros is likely to be brought; Venusaur offers more direct Tauros/Milotic pressure.

reflections.summary: Won because Whimsicott’s Prankster Tailwind, Encore, and Taunt controlled Charizard’s repeated Protects while Tauros’s Rock Slide supplied decisive pressure. The preview plan was less suitable than the piloting: Gholdengo was immediately exposed to sun-boosted Heat Wave, and Milotic never converted its anti-sun role before being overwhelmed.
reflections.adjustment: Next game, replace Gholdengo with Lum Berry Dragonite and lead Whimsicott-Tauros again; use Dragonite’s sleep protection, Tailwind, and pressure against the Charizard/Venusaur core while preserving Milotic for a safer sun response. No own Mega Stone holder or evolution was evidenced, so do not force a Mega plan without relevant information.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s revealed core relies on Mega Charizard-Y sun, Raichu Fake Out/Encore disruption, and Chlorophyll Venusaur Sleep Powder; Charizard also uses Protect repeatedly and Venusaur carries Focus Sash. Kingambit has Defiant, so avoid careless Intimidate-style support. Prefer Whimsicott-Tauros speed control, add Lum Berry Dragonite to absorb sleep and pressure sun teams, and avoid exposing Gholdengo directly to Charizard’s Heat Wave. Preserve Milotic for a deliberate Rain Dance or Hydro Pump response rather than using it as an early trade. No own Mega holder or evolution was established this game.
